answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can grow trust the way a vine climbs a trellis: a new identity starts with almost no weight and earns influence only by completing verifiable work over time, each job leaving a durable, checkable record. Reputation timber cannot simply be bought in bulk, because endorsements must come from distinct, long-standing peers whose own standing falls if they vouch for fakes, and voting or spending power stays capped until that history accumulates. Mass-produced copies therefore stay visibly rootless, while a real agent slowly climbs.
